How monthly payments are added up

Total paid = month 1 payment + month 2 payment + … + month 20 payment. Each month can have a different payment. In your small example, ₹100 minus ₹4 commission leaves ₹96, and ₹96 ÷ 20 = ₹4.80. If the next month’s payment is ₹5, the running total is ₹9.80. All 20 payments are added in the same way.

Blank monthly-payment fields automatically use that row’s amount received ÷ 20, rounded to paise. The calculated payment appears as a placeholder. Enter an actual payment to override it; clear the field to restore the automatic amount. Changing face value scales both bids and manually entered payments proportionally.

The same total of all 20 payments is used for every payout-month comparison. Chit cost paid = max(0, total paid − chosen payout). Net gain / loss = chosen payout + outside interest − total paid. The auction discount includes commission and is not charged again.

Months 1–19: payout = face value − bid, with commission included in the bid. Month 20: payout = face value − bid − commission. Commission is a percentage of face value. Use actual monthly-payment overrides if your scheme calculates installments differently.

Outside interest = payout × annual rate ÷ 12 × (20 − payout month) ÷ 100. The full payout stays lent out; interest does not compound and principal is returned at the end. Chit payments are funded separately. Month 20 has no remaining interest period. Net % = net gain / loss ÷ payout × 100; monthly net % = Net % ÷ 20; annual net % = monthly net % × 12. These are simple comparisons, not IRR. Rank 1 is the highest Net % and can still be a loss.

How these estimates work

EMI uses a fixed annual rate, monthly reducing-balance interest and month-end payments. Extra payments start in month one and shorten the term. Fees, taxes and penalties are excluded unless explicitly entered. Flat interest uses the original principal throughout. Loan comparison measures total cash paid, not APR or present value.

Chit figures cover one auction. Organizer commission is included in the auction discount; the remaining discount is shared equally among all members, including the winner. Members equal installments. Actual scheme rules can differ, and future discounts are unknown.
